text: matching the provided mock's style exactly

comments.text: P1 and A1 both hinge on "matching the mock", and the UI section adds "sentence case exactly as in the mock" — but the mock itself is only referenced, never attached or located. The ASCII sketch and the bullet list pin layout, text and approximate colours, but exact shades (the red, the light grey), corner radius and spacing are only in the external mock. Suggest listing the mock as an artifact (or attaching it to the spec) so a tester evaluating A1 has the same target the author had; otherwise "matches the mock" degrades to the tester's memory of an image the spec never captured.

text: The SUBMIT button is full card width, red, white uppercase text, rounded corners. The actual save rides the bean form's standard action row; the button is the mock's chrome.

comments.text: Clarifying question: the mock shows exactly one button, and P1 requires the form to match it, but the standard bean action row also renders its own save control. If both appear, the form no longer matches the mock exactly; if the action row is suppressed, the mock's SUBMIT is a dead button on a form whose only purpose is demonstrating form rendering. It would help to state which of the two the deliverable is (e.g. the SUBMIT chrome is the only visible button and the action row is hidden on this form, or the action row remains and P1 tolerates it), so A1 can be judged against a definite target.

text: IN: the form's style fidelity to the mock: rounded card, centred, field labels above inputs, full-width red SUBMIT.

comments.text: The latest edit dropped "centred" from P1 and A1 ("a white rounded card on a grey page"), but Scope still declares centring as IN and the Intent promises the mock "exactly". As written, a left-aligned card passes every criterion while violating the declared scope. Either restore centring to P1 and A1 ("a white rounded card centred on a grey page") or remove "centred" from the Scope line, so the scope and the verified requirement agree.

text: a full-width blue SUBMIT button with white uppercase text

comments.text: Colour changed by author request: the SUBMIT button is now blue (the theme's primary slot) in the layout, P1, A1, the UI section and Scope. The mock's red is superseded — the blue is the target A1 is judged against.

Superseded by a later author request: the button is now LOGIN, cyan with dark uppercase text, in the layout, P1, A1, Scope and the UI section. Cyan with dark text is the authoritative target A1 is judged against.

text: A1 (verifies P1): WHEN the form is opened, the system SHALL render a white rounded card centred on a grey page containing the two labelled inputs and the LOGIN button in the theme's info colour (the cyan-family slot), matching the mock's layout, colours and text

comments.text: A1 requires "matching the mock's ... colours and text", but P1 and the UI section now specify the button as "the theme's info colour" with "the theme's own contrast text" — an approximation of the mock, not a match (the mock's exact cyan and dark text are unreachable by a theme-slot layout). As written, a faithful implementation using the info slot could fail A1 on a literal reading, or pass it while a stricter tester fails the same render. Suggest wording A1's colour clause as "the LOGIN button in the theme's info colour, the platform's closest rendering of the mock's cyan" so the criterion judges the theme-slot target rather than the unreachable literal.

Superseded by a later author request: the button is now green — the theme's success slot — in the layout, P1, Scope, the UI section and A1. A1's colour clause already carries the suggested wording in its new form: "the theme's success colour (the green slot, the platform's closest rendering of the mock's green)" is the intended target, judged against the theme-slot rendering rather than an unreachable literal. Green is the authoritative target A1 is judged against.
